title: The Strait of Hormuz: the world's oil chokepoint
description: The 33 km-wide gate through which about a fifth of the world's oil passes, and the Gulf terminals that feed it.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration; Natural Earth

markers.label: Strait of Hormuz
markers.note: The narrowest point — 33 km wide, with two 3 km shipping lanes. ~20 million barrels of oil transit daily.

markers.label: Ras Tanura (Saudi Arabia)
markers.note: The world's largest offshore oil-loading terminal, on the Gulf's western shore.

markers.label: Kharg Island (Iran)
markers.note: Iran's main crude-export terminal, at the head of the Gulf.

markers.label: Fujairah (UAE)
markers.note: Bunkering and storage hub sitting just OUTSIDE the strait, on the Gulf of Oman.

markers.label: Ras Laffan (Qatar)
markers.note: One of the world's largest LNG export terminals — a third of seaborne LNG passes the strait.
